How a robot acts on what it sees

A warehouse robot uses sensors to read its surroundings. Software interprets those readings, plans a path and adjusts the motors as the robot moves. The same process applies to robots working in farms, hospitals and factories.

Mobile robots, arms and vision systems

The proposed projects are shown by year. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

  1. Year 1 Mobile robots

    Use sensor readings to steer a robot you build.

  2. Year 2 Robotic arms

    Build an arm and control its motion precisely.

  3. Year 3 Vision and navigation

    Work on vision systems, drones and self-driving platforms.

  4. Year 4 Robot learning

    Train a robot with data and simulation, then spend a semester in supervised engineering work.

Motion control, perception and simulation

The proposed curriculum combines programming and algorithms with mechatronics, embedded systems and motor control. Study kinematics and motion planning, then work with computer vision, machine learning, ROS 2 and simulation.

Where it leads

Explore work in robotics, industrial automation, machine perception, autonomous systems and drone technology. The course also offers a foundation for building a robotics company.

For those who want the detail

The projects bring together sensor readings, perception and motion control. Simulation lets you test how a robot behaves before evaluating it on a physical machine. In team builds, each student demonstrates their practical skills individually.

See how projects and skill tests work

Common questions

How much of the course involves coding?

Programming and algorithms are core skills. You also write software for sensors, controllers, motion planning and machine vision.

Do I need robotics experience to start?

The learning model starts with foundational skills and smaller builds. More complex projects follow as you practise programming, electronics and control.

Explore the robotics project sequence.

On your visit, ask how the proposed builds progress from a mobile robot to motion control, vision and simulation.
